verses.sa: कर्मणः सुकृतस्याहुः सात्त्विकं निर्मलं फलम् । रजसस्तु फलं दुःखमज्ञानं तमसः फलम् ॥
verses.tr: The result of wholesome action is pure and clear; the result of rajasic action is suffering; the result of tamasic action is ignorance and delusion.
verses.angle: Phalam: the fruit that matches the action
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Why do some actions leave us clear and others leave us in pain? Listen to how Krishna judges the result of every action.

body.text: The result of wholesome action is pure and clear; the result of rajasic action is suffering; the result of tamasic action is ignorance and delusion. The word phalam, fruit, appears three times in this verse. Krishna uses it to show that every action, whether good, restless, or dark, yields a specific fruit that matches its nature. Krishna now lists the fruits that arise directly from each of the three gunas.

verses.sa: सत्त्वात्सञ्जायते ज्ञानं रजसो लोभ एव च । प्रमादमोहौ तमसो भवतोऽज्ञानमेव च ॥
verses.tr: From sattva comes knowledge; from rajas, greed; from tamas, negligence, delusion, and ignorance.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna continues his teaching on the three gunas. Listen for the inner result that each one produces.

body.text: From sattva comes knowledge; from rajas, greed; from tamas, negligence, delusion, and ignorance. Each of the three gunas produces a specific inner result. Sattva gives birth to knowledge, while rajas gives birth to greed. Krishna then explains the direction of movement for those established in each of these three gunas.

verses.sa: ऊर्ध्वं गच्छन्ति सत्त्वस्था मध्ये तिष्ठन्ति राजसाः । जघन्यगुणवृत्तिस्था अधो गच्छन्ति तामसाः ॥
verses.tr: Those established in sattva go upward; those in rajas remain in the middle; those in the lowest movement of tamas go downward.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna offers a map of movement. Listen to how he pairs each guna with a direction.

body.text: Those established in sattva go upward; those in rajas remain in the middle; those in the lowest movement of tamas go downward. Krishna maps the three gunas onto directions. Sattva, sattvastha, means those established in sattva, and they move upward. Rajas, rajasa, means those in rajas, and they remain in the middle. Tamas, tamasa, means those in tamas, and they go downward. Krishna then says that the seer who knows the one beyond the gunas reaches his own being.

verses.sa: नान्यं गुणेभ्यः कर्तारं यदा द्रष्टानुपश्यति । गुणेभ्यश्च परं वेत्ति मद्भावं सोऽधिगच्छति ॥
verses.tr: When the seer understands that no doer exists apart from the three qualities, and knows the divine nature beyond them, that seer reaches my being.
verses.angle: The seer sees no doer beyond the gunas
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just described how the three qualities pull the embodied soul up or down, and now he turns to the one who sees through them. Listen to what that clear sight reveals.

body.text: When the seer understands that no doer exists apart from the three qualities, and knows the divine nature beyond them, that seer reaches my being. The verse names the seer who looks and sees clearly that there is no doer apart from the three qualities themselves. When that sight also reaches beyond the qualities into Krishna's own nature, the seer arrives at him. Krishna now goes on to say that the one who rises beyond these three qualities is freed from birth, death, and sorrow.

verses.tr: The embodied one who rises beyond these three qualities, which arise from the body, is freed from birth, death, old age, and sorrow, and attains immortality.
verses.angle: Amritam: the freedom the embodied one attains
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: The embodied one who rises beyond these three qualities, which arise from the body, is freed from birth, death, old age, and sorrow, and attains immortality.

body.text: The embodied one who rises beyond these three qualities, which arise from the body, is freed from birth, death, old age, and sorrow, and attains immortality. Here the word dehi, the embodied one, is the one who crosses beyond the qualities, and the reward is amritam, immortality, the freedom from birth, death, old age, and sorrow. Arjuna now asks, by what signs is a person known who has gone beyond these three qualities?

verses.sa: अर्जुन उवाचकैर्लिंगैस्त्रीन्गुणानेतानतीतो भवति प्रभो । किमाचारः कथं चैतांस्त्रीन्गुणानतिवर्तते ॥
verses.tr: Arjuna says: O Lord, by what signs is a person known who has gone beyond these three qualities? How does such a person behave, and how does one cross beyond the three qualities?
verses.angle: Arjuna asks three practical questions about the one beyond the gunas
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: If the wise can escape the three gunas, how do we know them, and how do we do the same? Listen to Arjuna’s three practical questions.

body.text: Arjuna says: O Lord, by what signs is a person known who has gone beyond these three qualities? How does such a person behave, and how does one cross beyond the three qualities? Arjuna asks three things in one breath: how to recognise the one beyond the gunas, how they act, and how to cross beyond them. He wants a sign he can see and a path he can walk. Krishna answers with the signs of a person who does not hate or long for the gunas.

verses.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचप्रकाशं च प्रवृत्तिं च मोहमेव च पाण्डव । न द्वेष्टि सम्प्रवृत्तानि न निवृत्तानि काङ्क्षति ॥
verses.tr: Krishna says: O Arjuna, the one who has gone beyond the three gunas does not hate light, activity, or confusion when they appear, and does not long for them when they disappear.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Arjuna asks for signs of a person beyond the gunas. Krishna answers with a test of even-mindedness, naming three states of mind.

body.text: Krishna says: O Arjuna, the one who has gone beyond the three gunas does not hate light, activity, or confusion when they appear, and does not long for them when they disappear. The word mohameva, delusion itself. Krishna places delusion on the same level as light and activity, showing that a steady mind meets confusion with the same calm as clarity. Krishna then describes the one who stands firm, knowing the gunas are only acting among themselves.

verses.sa: उदासीनवदासीनो गुणैर्यो न विचाल्यते । गुणा वर्तन्त इत्येव योऽवतिष्ठति नेङ्गते ॥
verses.tr: One who remains like an indifferent witness, unmoved by the three qualities, stands firm and does not stir, knowing only that the qualities are acting among themselves.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna points to a single posture to listen for in this verse, a way of sitting that shows the highest steadiness.

body.text: One who remains like an indifferent witness, unmoved by the three qualities, stands firm and does not stir, knowing only that the qualities are acting among themselves. The word to catch is asina, seated. He does not say the wise man is active or fighting the gunas; he says the man sits, still and uninvolved, while the gunas move around him. Next, Krishna shows how this steady one treats gold and a clod of earth as exactly the same.

verses.tr: The steady one remains equal in pleasure and pain, in a clod of earth, a stone, and gold; equal toward the liked and the disliked, toward praise and blame.
verses.angle: samaloshtashmakanchana, equal in dirt and gold
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna is showing Arjuna what a person who has gone beyond the three qualities looks like in everyday life. Listen for what they treat as exactly the same.

body.text: The steady one remains equal in pleasure and pain, in a clod of earth, a stone, and gold; equal toward the liked and the disliked, toward praise and blame. The steady one, the dhirah, sees a clod of earth, a stone, and gold as identical. The same equal mind covers praise and blame, because gold is just another object to be treated with indifference. Sanjaya answers with the king's own son, Duryodhana, looking across at the Pandava army.

verses.sa: मानापमानयोस्तुल्यस्तुल्यो मित्रारिपक्षयोः । सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी गुणातीतः स उच्यते ॥
verses.tr: The steady one is equal in honor and dishonor, equal toward friend and foe, and has abandoned all undertakings. Such a person is called beyond the three gunas.
verses.angle: sarvarambhaparityagi: abandoning the root of action
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna carries on by naming the final pair of opposites that the steady one meets with the same evenness.

body.text: The steady one is equal in honor and dishonor, equal toward friend and foe, and has abandoned all undertakings. Such a person is called beyond the three gunas. The word sarvarambhaparityagi, one who has abandoned all beginnings of action, shows that the person beyond the gunas no longer starts deeds from personal craving, but lets go of the very root of action. Next, Krishna continues.

verses.sa: मां च योऽव्यभिचारेण भक्ितयोगेन सेवते । स गुणान्समतीत्यैतान् ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते ॥
verses.tr: Whoever serves Me with unwavering devotion transcends these qualities and becomes fit for union with the supreme reality.
verses.angle: Steady devotion can carry you beyond the forces that shape ordinary life.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: What is the exact way to rise above the forces that bind human behavior? Listen closely to how devotion is described.

body.text: Whoever serves Me with unwavering devotion transcends these qualities and becomes fit for union with the supreme reality. The word sevate simply means serves. It is a steady action of serving the supreme, and this serving directly causes one to cross over the qualities. Krishna then reveals that he himself is the very foundation of this highest reality and the eternal bliss it holds.

verses.sa: ब्रह्मणो हि प्रतिष्ठाऽहममृतस्याव्ययस्य च । शाश्वतस्य च धर्मस्य सुखस्यैकान्तिकस्य च ॥
verses.tr: For I am the foundation of Brahman, of immortality, of the imperishable, of eternal dharma, and of unending bliss.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna closes this chapter by naming the ground beneath everything. Listen for the word that holds up all of existence.

body.text: For I am the foundation of Brahman, of immortality, of the imperishable, of eternal dharma, and of unending bliss. The verse rests on one word, pratishtha, meaning foundation or support. Krishna is not merely a part of the world; he is the base upon which Brahman, immortality, and ultimate bliss all stand. Krishna now turns to the cosmic tree, with its roots above and its branches below. Listen to how he describes its shape.

next.title: The tree with its roots above
